increments.title: Content-bearing telemetry is captured by default and served over the API
increments.goal: Turn the content flags on by default in `argus env` and make the collector store and serve what the resulting events carry, so a caller can ask for the conversation content belonging to a point in time.
criteria: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in both output formats: user prompts, tool details, tool content, and the flag or flags the CLI requires to emit `api_request_body`/`api_response_body` events.
The exact flag names are verified against the CLI's monitoring documentation rather than assumed.
If the current CLI turns out not to emit request/response body events at all, that is reported as an explicit finding, naming the best content the available flags do provide.
What attribution actually arrives for subagent activity and for request bodies is established and reported, including any gap, so later increments know which records can be assigned to which agent.

The collector stores the content those events carry and exposes those content-bearing records over the JSON API like the existing signals, such that the content belonging to a point in time can be asked for.
Recordings made without the content flags are out of contract: no fallback rendering, no compatibility notice, and no test pins behavior for them.
`./test.sh` is green.

return.summary: Turn the four content flags on in `otelEnvFor` (the CLI's flag for request/response bodies is OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES, verified in the installed CLI 2.1.224 binary), classify content-bearing log events in claude.mjs, add store.queryContent plus GET /api/content with an `at` bound, and keep the raw body out of /api/events; bodies carry query_source and span context but no agent.name or agent_id, which is the attribution gap later increments must join through spans.
return.plan:
## What the CLI actually does (verified, not assumed)

Verified twice: against the monitoring documentation at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage (read 2026-08-07) and against the installed Claude Code binary at /opt/claude-code/bin/claude, version 2.1.224 (`claude --version`). The npm copy at /opt/node22/lib/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code is a stale 2.1.42 and was not used. Strings quoted below come from the 2.1.224 binary.

1. **The flag for request/response bodies is `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES`.** It exists in the binary and gates the emit path: `PFd()` reads `process.env.OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES`, `MO_()` maps `1`/true to `{mode:'inline'}` and `file:<dir>` to `{mode:'file'}`, anything else to `{mode:'disabled'}`. So the CLI does emit `claude_code.api_request_body` and `claude_code.api_response_body`: the finding the criteria ask for as a fallback ("the CLI cannot emit bodies at all") does not apply.
2. **Set it to `1` (inline), not `file:<dir>`.** In file mode the CLI writes `<dir>/<id>.request.json` on the agent's own disk and the event carries only `body_ref` plus `body_length` — the collector would receive a path it cannot read whenever the agent is not on the collector's machine. Inline mode puts the body in the event, which is the only mode that makes the collector the store. Rejected: file mode, and rejected: setting `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH` to raise the 60 KB truncation ceiling — no criterion asks for it and the ceiling exists because backends cap attribute values at 64 KB.
3. **Inline body events carry exactly:** `body` (JSON string, truncated at the content limit, 61440 UTF-16 code units by default, with `body_truncated: "true"` when it was), `body_length` (untruncated length), `model`, `query_source`, plus what every event gets from the emitter `vu()`: the standard attributes (`session.id`, `user.*`, `organization.id`, `terminal.type`, resource attributes), `event.name`, `event.timestamp`, `event.sequence`, and `prompt.id` when a prompt is active. `api_response_body` additionally carries `request_id`. Extended-thinking blocks in the request's prior assistant turns are replaced with `<REDACTED>` by the CLI before serialisation.
4. **Attribution — the gap, established.** The emit site is `oBo(request, i.querySource)` → `OFd('api_request_body', body, { model, query_source })`. It does **not** call the attribution builder `ahr()`, which is what attaches `agent.name`, `skill.name`, `plugin.name`, `marketplace.name`, `mcp_server.name`, `mcp_tool.name`. Only `api_request` (via the metric path `Lye`), `api_error` and `api_refusal` call it. So **no body event carries `agent.name`, and no log event of any kind carries `agent_id`**: `tool_result` is emitted as `vu('tool_result', {...}, n.agentContext)` and that third argument is folded by `mtn()` into `workflow.run_id`/`workflow.name` only. What bodies do carry for attribution:
   - `query_source`, passed through raw: `repl_main_thread` (and `repl_main_thread:outputStyle:*`), `sdk`, `agent:builtin:<type>`, `agent:custom:<name>`, `agent:default`, `agent:custom`, `compact`, `hook_agent`, `hook_prompt`, `side_question`, `web_search_tool`, and similar. This names the agent **type**, never the agent instance: two concurrent subagents of the same type produce identical `query_source`.
   - Span context. `vu()` calls `AAy()`, which returns the active OTel context when a valid span context is on it, and attaches it to the log record — so body events arrive with `traceId`/`spanId` set (argus already keeps both, see decode.mjs `normalizeLogs`). `claude_code.llm_request` and `claude_code.tool` spans carry `agent_id` and `parent_agent_id` (absent on the main session). **The join from a body to a concrete agent instance therefore runs body.spanId → span → span.attrs.agent_id, and needs traces switched on.** `argus env` already sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1` and `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp` by default, so that path is available; with `--traces false` it is not, and only `query_source` remains.
   - `prompt.id` groups every event of one interaction, and `event.sequence` orders events within a session. Both are already carried through by the decoder as plain attributes.
   This is the whole attribution finding for later increments: lanes can be built per agent instance from spans, bodies can be assigned to a lane through their span, and where a body has no span it can only be assigned to an agent type.
5. **`OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES` is deliberately not set.** The binary reads it as `ee.OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES ?? ee.OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, so setting user prompts already turns assistant response text on. None of my criteria names it, and one variable that means one thing beats two that can disagree.

## What gets built

### 1. `otelEnvFor` turns the content flags on (src/claude.mjs)

Add to the base `env` object, unconditionally — not behind the `traces` option and not behind a new option:

```
OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS: '1',
OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS: '1',
OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT: '1',
OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES: '1',
```

`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT` only does anything with tracing on, but it is inert otherwise, and tying it to the `traces` option would make the content block depend on an unrelated switch. Rejected: an `--content` opt-in or a `--no-content` opt-out — decision 1 of the issue chose "on by default" over an opt-in, and an opt-out was never decided; anyone who wants them off unsets the variables. All four output formats (`shell`, `json`, `dotenv`, `settings`) render the same object through `renderEnv`, so this one change covers every format the CLI offers.

### 2. Content classification (src/claude.mjs)

Add one exported helper next to the other domain knowledge, so no other module string-matches attribute names:

```
export function contentOf(log) -> null | {
  kind: 'request_body' | 'response_body' | 'user_prompt' | 'assistant_response' | 'tool_input',
  text: string | null,      // what the event actually carried, null in file mode
  length: number,           // untruncated length the CLI reported, else text.length, else 0
  truncated: boolean,       // body_truncated === 'true'
  ref: string | null,       // body_ref path, null unless the CLI ran in file mode
}
```

Mapping, by `log.eventName`:
- `claude_code.api_request_body` → `request_body`; text `attrs.body`, length `num(attrs.body_length)`, truncated `bool(attrs.body_truncated)`, ref `attrs.body_ref ?? null`.
- `claude_code.api_response_body` → `response_body`; same attributes.
- `claude_code.user_prompt` → `user_prompt`; text `attrs.prompt`, length `num(attrs.prompt_length)`.
- `claude_code.assistant_response` → `assistant_response`; text `attrs.response`, length `num(attrs.response_length)`.
- `claude_code.tool_result` → `tool_input`; text `attrs.tool_input ?? attrs.tool_parameters` (the existing `toolParametersOf` doc comment records why both names), length `num(attrs.tool_input_size_bytes)`.

Any other event name, or one of these with neither a text nor a `body_ref`, returns `null`. **No redaction handling:** a `<REDACTED>` value is treated as ordinary text. That is deliberate — criterion "recordings without the content flags are out of contract" forbids a fallback, and special-casing the redaction marker would be exactly that.

Careful: a log record has both a top-level `body` field (the OTLP LogRecord body, here the string `claude_code.api_request_body`) and an `attrs.body` attribute (the payload). `contentOf` reads `attrs`, never the record's own `body`.

### 3. `queryContent` on the store (src/store.mjs)

```
queryContent({ sessionId = null, kinds = null, atMs = null, limit = 100 } = {}) -> Array<{ log, content }>
```

Written exactly like the existing `queryEvents`: walk `this.logs` from the newest backwards, skip anything `contentOf` returns null for, skip on `sessionId`, on `kinds` (an array of kind names) and on `atMs` (keep only `log.timeMs <= atMs`, inclusive), stop at `limit`, then `reverse()` so the result is oldest-first. Consequence worth stating: `atMs` plus `limit: 1` returns the nearest content record at or before that time, which is the query later increments need for "the context as of this moment".

Rejected: a parallel index array or a per-session map of content records. Both would have to be kept in step with `#trim` and `#dropSession`, and buy nothing over the same linear scan `/api/events` already does on every request. No new storage: `#applyLog` already pushes every log into `this.logs` with its attributes intact, and `persist.mjs` already writes every record whole, so bodies are stored and persisted with no change to either.

### 4. `GET /api/content` (src/server.mjs)

In `handleApi`, beside `/api/events`:

- Query parameters: `session` (session id, optional), `kind` (comma-separated kind names, optional), `at` (epoch milliseconds, optional, inclusive upper bound), `limit` (default 100, max 500, via the existing `intParam`), `body` (`1` to include the text).
- Response: `{ items: [...] }`, oldest-first, each item:

```
{
  seq, timeMs, sessionId, traceId, spanId, eventName,
  kind, length, truncated, ref,
  model: attrs.model ?? null,
  querySource: attrs.query_source ?? null,
  requestId: attrs.request_id ?? null,
  attribution: attributionOf(attrs),
  storedLength: text ? text.length : 0,
  text            // present only when body=1; null when the event carried only a ref
}
```

Text is opt-in because a hundred inline bodies are six megabytes; a caller that wants one body asks for one. `attributionOf` is reused unchanged — it already picks up `query_source` and `model`.

### 5. `/api/events` stops shipping raw bodies

Turning the flags on by default makes the existing event tail enormous: `/api/events` returns whole records, and a page of 200 events can now contain dozens of 60 KB bodies on every poll. In the `/api/events` mapping only, drop the `body` attribute of `claude_code.api_request_body` and `claude_code.api_response_body` items, keeping `body_length`, `body_truncated` and everything else; full text stays available at `/api/content?body=1`. Build a copy — `{ ...event, attrs: { ...event.attrs, body: undefined } }` or an equivalent — and never `delete` on the stored record, which would destroy the stored content. No other event kind is touched: `tool_input` and `prompt` are bounded by the CLI's own per-value limits and the existing UI reads them.

### 6. README (tools/argus/README.md)

Three passages become false or incomplete and are corrected in the same change:
- "Sensitive data" (~line 503) currently states `argus env` deliberately does **not** set these flags. Replace with: it now sets all four by default, name them, and state the consequence — prompts, tool arguments and whole conversation bodies live in the collector's memory and, with `--persist`, in the measurement directory.
- The "Wiring up an agent" example block (~line 68) must show the four new exports.
- The HTTP API table (~line 536) gets a `GET /api/content` row with its parameters.

## Facts the later increments need, and things deliberately left alone

- `tools/argus-ui/src/server.mjs` proxies every path under `/api/` (its `PROXIED` predicate), so `/api/content` is reachable from the UI without any change there. No file in `tools/argus-ui` is touched by this increment.
- `tools/argus-ui/public/app.js` still tells the user to set `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` themselves (around line 398); that hint is stale after this change but the UI belongs to a later increment.
- `scripts/demo-emit.mjs` emits no content-bearing events, so the synthetic demo produces nothing for `/api/content`. Left as is — no criterion asks for it — and named here because the UI increments will want a fixture.
- Persistence rotates each signal at 64 MB and keeps two generations, so a measurement retains roughly 128 MB of log JSONL — on the order of two thousand 60 KB bodies. A long session replayed with `--open` will therefore have lost its earliest bodies. Left unchanged: it is the same order as the in-memory bound of 50,000 log records, and raising it trades a disk for a memory problem. Reported so a later increment can decide.
- No byte budget is added to the in-memory log window. It stays bounded by count (`--max-logs`, default 50,000) and age; with bodies on, that window can hold hundreds of megabytes. Rejected an eviction pass that strips old bodies: it would make `/api/events` and `/api/content` disagree about the same record and no criterion asks for it. The README's Limits section is where `--max-logs` is named as the lever.
- `describeEvent` is not extended for the body events; they fall through to the default branch, which returns the record's own body string (`claude_code.api_request_body`) — short, correct, and not the payload.

Node v22.22.2 is installed and the packages are zero-dependency by design: no `npm install` runs anywhere, and there is no build step. There is no linter and no formatter in this repository — nothing to run for style.

Commands this plan asks anyone to run, all from the repository root /home/user/uroboros:
- `node --test tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs` — one test file.
- `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs` — one test file.
- `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs` — one test file; binds real servers on port 0.
- `node --test tools/argus/test/env.test.mjs` — one test file; spawns `node tools/argus/bin/argus.mjs env`, which prints and exits without opening a port.
- `npm --prefix tools/argus test` — the whole argus suite, `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`, which picks up a newly added test file automatically.
- `./test.sh` — every suite in the repository: test-repo.sh, test-worktree.sh (creates git worktrees), the backlog recorder, tools/argus, tools/argus-ui, tools/log-parser.

Tests are needed. Everything below is the whole work order; the framework everywhere is `node:test` with `node:assert/strict`, ESM `.mjs`, no helper library.

## Case group A — `argus env` carries the content flags (criterion 1)

File: /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs (unit). Conventions of that file: no describe blocks; each `test('sentence describing the fact', () => {...})` names the fact rather than the function; assertions are `assert.equal`/`assert.ok` on the object `otelEnvFor` returns; the existing cases carry a short comment saying *why* the fact matters, and that style is expected of new ones.

A1. **The env block turns the content flags on by default.** Input: `otelEnvFor('http://localhost:4318')`. State: none. Expected: `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT` and `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES` are each exactly the string `'1'`. `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES` must be `'1'` and not a `file:` value — inline is what makes the body reach the collector.

A2. **The content flags do not ride on the traces opt-in.** Input: `otelEnvFor('http://localhost:4318', { traces: false })`. Expected: the same four variables are still `'1'`, while `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` is absent (the existing behaviour of the `traces` option).

Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs`

## Case group B — every output format of `argus env` (criterion 1, "both output formats")

File: /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/test/env.test.mjs — a new file. There is no test for the `env` command today; copy the subprocess conventions of /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/test/version.test.mjs: a module-level `const BIN = fileURLToPath(new URL('../bin/argus.mjs', import.meta.url))`, a `runArgus(args, {cwd, env})` helper built on `promisify(execFile)` with `timeout: 10_000` and `encoding: 'utf8'` that resolves to `{stdout, stderr, code}` for both success and failure instead of rejecting, and a file-header comment saying what the criteria fix. Do not assert any wall-clock duration: /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/CLAUDE.md forbids it and the per-command timeout is the only clock. Run the CLI with `env: { UROBOROS_OBS_PORT: '4318' }` so the printed endpoint does not depend on the machine's environment.

B1. **Every format carries all four content flags.** Input: run `env`, `env --format json`, `env --format dotenv`, `env --format settings` — one case looping over the four, or four cases, whichever reads better. State: none; `argus env` starts no collector. Expected, per format: exit code 0, and each of the four variables present with the value `1` — in the `shell` output as the line `export OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES="1"` (and likewise for the other three), in `dotenv` as `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1`, in `json` as a top-level key of `JSON.parse(stdout)` whose value is `'1'`, in `settings` as a key of `JSON.parse(stdout).env` whose value is `'1'`. Parse the JSON forms rather than matching text on them.

Edge deliberately covered here: `settings` is the format whose keys sit one level down under `env`, which is the only way this rendering can go wrong per-format.

Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus/test/env.test.mjs`

## Case group C — classifying a content-bearing event (criterion 5)

File: /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs (unit), same conventions as group A. The subject is the new `contentOf(log)`, which takes a normalized log record `{ eventName, attrs, ... }` and returns `null` or `{ kind, text, length, truncated, ref }`.

C1. **An inline request body is classified with its untruncated length.** Input: `{ eventName: 'claude_code.api_request_body', attrs: { body: '{"messages":[]}', body_length: '61440', body_truncated: 'true', model: 'claude-opus-5', query_source: 'agent:builtin:researcher' } }`. Expected: `kind === 'request_body'`, `text` is the exact `body` string, `length === 61440` (a number, though the CLI sends it as a string), `truncated === true`, `ref === null`.

C2. **A body the CLI wrote to a file is classified by its reference, with no text.** Input: the same event name with `attrs: { body_ref: '/tmp/bodies/abc.request.json', body_length: '120000' }` and no `body`. Expected: `kind === 'request_body'`, `text === null`, `ref` is the path, `length === 120000`, `truncated === false`.

C3. **A response body is its own kind.** Input: `{ eventName: 'claude_code.api_response_body', attrs: { body: '{"id":"msg_1"}', body_length: '13', request_id: 'req_1' } }`. Expected: `kind === 'response_body'`, `text` is the body string.

C4. **Prompt, assistant response and tool input are content too.** Three inputs, one case or three: `claude_code.user_prompt` with `{ prompt: 'hello', prompt_length: '5' }` → `kind === 'user_prompt'`, `text === 'hello'`, `length === 5`; `claude_code.assistant_response` with `{ response: 'hi', response_length: '2' }` → `kind === 'assistant_response'`; `claude_code.tool_result` with `{ tool_name: 'Read', tool_input: '{"file":"a"}', tool_input_size_bytes: '12' }` → `kind === 'tool_input'`, `text` is the JSON string.

C5. **The older attribute name for tool input is still read.** Input: `claude_code.tool_result` with `tool_parameters` instead of `tool_input`. Expected: `kind === 'tool_input'` and the text comes from `tool_parameters`. This mirrors the fallback `toolParametersOf` already documents for CLI versions before 2.1.x renamed it.

C6. **An event that carries no content at all is not content.** Input: `{ eventName: 'claude_code.api_request', attrs: { model: 'claude-opus-5', input_tokens: 10 } }`. Expected: `null`. Use `api_request` and no other event: it carries no content under any configuration, so this case says "this kind of event is not content" and not "the flags were off", which nothing here may pin.

Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs`

## Case group D — asking the store for content at a point in time (criterion 5)

File: /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs (unit). Conventions of that file: a module-level `const SESSION = 'sess-1'`, factory helpers `metric(...)`, `log(eventName, attributes = {}, timeMs = Date.now())` and `span(...)` at the top that build normalized records with `attrs: { 'session.id': SESSION, ...attributes }`; each case constructs `new TelemetryStore()`, calls `store.ingest('logs', [...])` and asserts on the query result; nothing is mocked and no server is involved. Records must sit near `Date.now()` — the store evicts anything older than the retention window on ingest, which the file's own comment records. Use a local `const T = Date.now()` and offsets of a few seconds.

D1. **Content records come back oldest-first, only for the session asked for.** State: ingest into one store an `api_request_body` at `T` for `SESSION`, an `api_request_body` at `T + 1000` for a second session id, a `user_prompt` with a `prompt` at `T + 2000` for `SESSION`, and an `api_request` (no content) at `T + 3000` for `SESSION`. Input: `store.queryContent({ sessionId: SESSION })`. Expected: two results, in the order body-then-prompt, each carrying the log record and the classification (`kind` `'request_body'` then `'user_prompt'`); the other session's body and the contentless `api_request` are absent.

D2. **The kind filter narrows to one kind.** Same state. Input: `store.queryContent({ sessionId: SESSION, kinds: ['request_body'] })`. Expected: one result, the body at `T`.

D3. **`atMs` is an inclusive upper bound.** State: bodies at `T`, `T + 1000` and `T + 2000`. Input: `store.queryContent({ sessionId: SESSION, atMs: T + 1000 })`. Expected: two results — the record exactly at the bound is included, the later one is not.

D4. **The nearest content at or before a time is `atMs` with `limit: 1`.** Same state as D3. Input: `store.queryContent({ sessionId: SESSION, kinds: ['request_body'], atMs: T + 1500, limit: 1 })`. Expected: exactly one result, the record at `T + 1000` — the limit keeps the newest match, not the oldest. This is the query the later increments build the context view on, so it is pinned here.

D5. **A session with nothing content-bearing answers with an empty list.** State: ingest only an `api_request` event. Input: `store.queryContent({ sessionId: SESSION })`. Expected: an empty array, not null and not a throw.

Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`

## Case group E — the content API over HTTP (criterion 5)

File: /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs (integration). Conventions of that file: the `withServer(options, run)` helper builds a real `TelemetryStore` and `createServer({ store, endpoint: 'http://test', log: () => {} })`, listens on port 0 — never a fixed port, which /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/CLAUDE.md requires — and hands the case `{ base, store }`; cases drive it with `fetch` against `${base}/...`; payloads are built as OTLP/JSON strings by a local factory (see `logsPayloadJson`) or as protobuf via `encodeMessage`; the POST's own status is asserted before anything is read back, so a failed ingest reports as a failed ingest. Add a local payload factory for content events in the same shape as `logsPayloadJson`, with `attributes` as OTLP `{ key, value: { stringValue } }` pairs and `timeUnixNano` as a decimal string.

E1. **Content-bearing records are listed over the API, without their text by default.** State: POST to `/v1/logs` one OTLP/JSON payload for session `s-content` holding an `api_request_body` (attributes `body` = a recognisable JSON string, `body_length`, `model`, `query_source: 'agent:builtin:researcher'`) at `T`, an `api_response_body` at `T + 500`, and a `user_prompt` with a `prompt` at `T + 1000`; assert that POST returned 200. Input: `GET ${base}/api/content?session=s-content`. Expected: 200, `items.length === 3`, oldest-first, kinds `['request_body', 'response_body', 'user_prompt']`; the first item carries `timeMs`, `length`, `truncated === false`, `querySource === 'agent:builtin:researcher'` and `attribution.query_source === 'agent:builtin:researcher'`; and it carries no `text` — assert the absence, since text is the opt-in.

E2. **The content at a point in time is one request away.** Same state, with a second `api_request_body` at `T + 2000` carrying a different body string. Input: `GET ${base}/api/content?session=s-content&kind=request_body&at=<T+1500>&limit=1&body=1`. Expected: 200, exactly one item, `text` equal to the first body string exactly, `kind === 'request_body'`.

E3. **The event tail no longer carries whole bodies.** Same state. Input: `GET ${base}/api/events?session=s-content`. Expected: the `api_request_body` item is present in `items` and its `attrs.body_length` is intact, while `attrs.body` is absent; and afterwards `GET ${base}/api/content?session=s-content&kind=request_body&limit=1&body=1` still returns the full text — proving the stored record was copied, not stripped.

Edges covered here: a request without `session` (E4) and a bad `at`. E4. **Asking without a session asks across all of them, and a bad `at` is ignored rather than fatal.** Input: `GET ${base}/api/content` and `GET ${base}/api/content?session=s-content&at=nonsense`. Expected: both 200, both listing the session's content records (`intParam` already falls back on an unparseable value; assert the fallback, not an error).

Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`

## What is left untested, and why

- **Recordings made without the content flags.** Out of contract by the increment's own criterion. No case asserts what happens to a `user_prompt` without a `prompt`, to a `<REDACTED>` value, or to any pre-change measurement directory. Case C6 deliberately uses `claude_code.api_request` — an event that carries no content in any configuration — so that the negative case cannot be read as pinning flagless behaviour.
- **That the CLI really emits these events with these flags.** Not runnable inside the suite: it needs a live Claude Code process. It was established instead by reading the installed 2.1.224 binary and the monitoring documentation, and the findings are in the plan.
- **README prose.** No test; a reader checks it.
- **Persistence of bodies.** The persistence path is unchanged — it serialises whole records already — and test/persist.test.mjs covers that round trip. Adding a body-shaped fixture there would re-test the same code.
- **Memory behaviour with large bodies.** No bound was added, so there is nothing to assert; the consequence is documented in the README's Limits section.
- **`tools/argus-ui`.** Untouched by this increment; its proxy already forwards `/api/*`.

return.summary:
Opening cut of the argus timeline issue into six increments, all todo, within the run's budget of eight.

Where each acceptance criterion landed. Criterion 1 (`argus env` carries the content flags, flag names verified) and criterion 2 (the collector stores and serves content-bearing records over the JSON API) both went to `content-pipeline`: turning the flags on delivers nothing until the collector keeps what arrives, and the collector cannot be shaped without knowing what the flags actually make the CLI emit, so they are one change. Criterion 9 (recordings without the content flags are out of contract, nothing tests them) is recorded there too, because the collector is the one place tempted to write a fallback; it is a standing prohibition that every later increment's review re-applies. Criterion 10 (`./test.sh` green) is likewise recorded on `content-pipeline` so the gate binds from the first increment onward, and every increment must leave it green as the price of standing on its own. Criterion 3 (the session opens on the timeline, technical views subordinate) and criterion 4 (a lane per agent, spanning its lifetime) went to `timeline-landing`. Criterion 5 (activity plus a context-size curve per lane) is `lane-activity`. Criterion 6 (scrub plus live mode) is `scrub-live`. Criterion 7 (context as a structured, expandable message list) is `context-at-time`. Criterion 8 (tools used up to that moment, with parameters) is `tools-at-time`.

Why this order. `content-pipeline` is first because it is both the load-bearing one and the one carrying the run's open questions: the exact flag names, whether the CLI emits request/response bodies at all, and how completely subagent traffic is attributed. Every UI increment depends on the answers, and if bodies turn out not to be emittable the later cut has to change — so the run has to learn that before it draws anything. I made those unknowns explicit criteria of that increment rather than questions for the human, because the issue already tells the researcher to verify them against the CLI's documentation and against the telemetry itself; nothing here needs a human decision, so `questions` is empty. Then the timeline is built outside in: the view and its lanes, the drawing inside the lanes, the time control, and finally the two detail panels that need a chosen time to mean anything.

What I rejected. Splitting the `argus env` flags from the collector work — half of it is a config change nobody can judge. Merging `timeline-landing` with `lane-activity` — that one increment would carry the whole navigation restructure plus the lane rendering plus the context-size curve, too much for a single review, while "the session opens on a timeline that shows which agents ran when" is already judgeable on its own. Merging `context-at-time` with `tools-at-time` — they share the selection and the chosen time, but the message list with per-block sizes and expansion is substantial on its own, and the two answer different questions from the issue ("what fills the context" versus "which tools, and what for"); splitting them costs one extra chain and keeps both reviewable, with the tool list riding on selection plumbing the context increment will already have.

One fact the cut turns on that I do not have: how completely the telemetry attributes subagent activity. If attribution is thin, `timeline-landing` may deliver fewer lanes than hoped. Rather than guess, `content-pipeline` is cut to answer it first and report the gap, and I will re-cut the lane increments against that finding on the next call.
